annotations.title: Which base images in this Dockerfile are out of support?

description: Paste a whole Dockerfile. Returns every FROM line whose base image is a Python, Node.js or Ubuntu release this register holds, with that release's end-of-active-support and end-of-security-support dates, whether it is past either one today, and a verbatim quote of the vendor's own published line. Every FROM line it could NOT answer for — another product, a `latest` or build-argument tag, a bare digest, an earlier build stage — comes back in `not_in_our_records` or `unresolvable` with the reason in words, and is counted in `images_unresolved`. An empty `out_of_support` list with a non-zero `images_unresolved` does NOT mean the file is clean.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile text. Multi-stage files, `--platform` flags, `AS` stage names, comments, registry prefixes and digest pins are all handled; nothing else in the file is read.

name: check_dockerfile

from_lines.description: FROM lines found in the file.

images_checked.description: FROM lines matched to a release in this register.

images_unresolved.description: FROM lines not checked. See not_in_our_records and unresolvable.

not_in_our_records.description: FROM lines this tool could not answer for. Read this before reporting a Dockerfile clean: these lines were NOT checked, which is not the same as being in support.

out_of_support.description: Checked images past end of security support, soonest-expired first.

also_reported.description: Values for this record reported by a SECOND source, each with its own source_url and source_quote. Cite these to the page they name, never to the record's primary source.

covered_by_paid_extended_support.description: OURS, computed: true when free security support has ended but the paid Ubuntu Pro window has not. A caller without Ubuntu Pro should read this as unsupported.

end_of_active_support.description: The source's eoasFrom date, verbatim. Bug fixes stop here.

end_of_security_support.description: The source's eolFrom date, verbatim. The free security-patch path stops here. This is the date the status is read from.

extended_security_maintenance.description: Ubuntu only: the source's eoesFrom date, verbatim. Expanded Security Maintenance needs a paid Ubuntu Pro subscription, so it is NOT treated as support when computing the status.

product.description: The product name as the source writes it: "Python", "Node.js" or "Ubuntu".

record_url.description: This record's own page on referencesource.org.

release.description: The release label exactly as the source writes it, e.g. "3.11", "24.04 'Noble Numbat' (LTS)".

released.description: Release date, verbatim from the source.

source_quote.description: Verbatim text from that page containing the value.

source_url.description: The page the value was read from.

status.description: OURS, computed against the date of the call: "supported", "past end of active support", "past end of security support", or "no end-of-support date published". The dates above are the vendor's.

status_basis.description: OURS: which date the status was read from, "eol" or "eoas".

vendor_names_for_these_dates.description: The source's own labels object, verbatim.

past_active_support.description: Checked images still getting security fixes but no longer bug fixes.
